class.name: EditorExportPlatformWeb
class.description: The Web exporter customizes how a web build is handled. In the editor's "Export" window, it is created when adding a new "Web" preset. [b]Note:[/b] Godot on Web is rendered inside a [code]<canvas>[/code] tag. Normally, the canvas cannot be positioned or resized manually, but otherwise acts as the main [Window] of the application.

members.member: File path to the custom export template used for debug builds. If left empty, the default template is used.
File path to the custom export template used for release builds. If left empty, the default template is used.

Determines how the canvas should be resized by Godot. - [b]None:[/b] The canvas is not automatically resized. - [b]Project:[/b] The size of the canvas is dependent on the [ProjectSettings]. - [b]Adaptive:[/b] The canvas is automatically resized to fit as much of the web page as possible.

The custom HTML page that wraps the exported web build. If left empty, the default HTML shell is used. For more information, see the [url=$DOCS_URL/tutorials/platform/web/customizing_html5_shell.html]Customizing HTML5 Shell[/url] tutorial.

The origins of the pages allowed to drive [member html/embed_fullscreen/enabled], separated by commas, for example [code]https://lms.example.edu, https://site.example.com[/code]: scheme, host and port, with no path. Messages from a parent page on any other origin are ignored. Leave it empty to accept any page that embeds the game. Only used while [member html/embed_fullscreen/enabled] is [code]true[/code].
If [code]true[/code], embeds support for a virtual keyboard into the web page, which is shown when necessary on touchscreen devices.
If [code]true[/code], the project icon will be used as the favicon for this application's web page.
If [code]true[/code], the canvas will be focused as soon as the application is loaded, if the browser window is already in focus.

If [code]true[/code], the first tap on the canvas puts the page in fullscreen on phones and tablets (devices whose primary pointer is a touchscreen). Browsers only lock the screen orientation in fullscreen, so this is what makes [member html/orientation] apply without any code in the project. Desktop browsers are unaffected. If the player leaves fullscreen, it is not entered again.

Additional HTML tags to include inside the [code]<head>[/code], such as [code]<meta>[/code] tags. [b]Note:[/b] You do not need to add a [code]<title>[/code] tag, as it is automatically included based on the project's name.

The screen orientation the exported project runs in on phones and tablets. [b]Project Setting[/b] follows [member ProjectSettings.display/window/handheld/orientation]; any other value overrides that setting in the exported project. The progressive web app manifest uses the same orientation. Browsers only allow the orientation to be locked while the page is in fullscreen (or runs as an installed progressive web app), so the engine requests the lock again every time the page enters fullscreen: on the first tap with [member html/fullscreen_on_first_tap], or through [method DisplayServer.window_set_mode] called from an input event. Desktop browsers do not lock the orientation, and report [constant DisplayServer.FEATURE_ORIENTATION] as unsupported.

The Start button's background color. Unless [member html/start_button/custom_state_colors] is [code]true[/code], the button is drawn 15% darker while the pointer is over it and 30% darker while it is pressed. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].
The color of the Start button's border. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].
The radius of the Start button's corners, in CSS pixels. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].
The width of the Start button's border, in CSS pixels. [code]0[/code] draws no border. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the Start button uses [member html/start_button/hover_color] while the pointer is over it and [member html/start_button/pressed_color] while it is pressed. If [code]false[/code], it uses [member html/start_button/background_color] darkened by 15% and 30%. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the exported page opens on a start screen: the boot splash with a Start button under it. Nothing of the engine runs until the button is pressed: the engine is not compiled, and no GPU device or audio context is created. Its files download in the background meanwhile unless [member html/start_button/preload] is [code]false[/code]. Pressing it runs the usual startup, with the same loading screen. The press counts as a user gesture inside the page, so the game's audio can start without waiting for another click. The button is a real HTML button: it shows a focus ring when reached with [kbd]Tab[/kbd] and is pressed with [kbd]Enter[/kbd] or [kbd]Space[/kbd]. It is not focused when the page loads, since inside an iframe that would scroll the parent page to the game. A browser that lacks a required feature (such as WebGPU) shows the error at once instead of the button. A custom HTML shell receives these settings as [code]startButton[/code] in [code]$GODOT_CONFIG[/code]. Default: [code]false[/code].
The Start button's font, as a CSS [code]font-family[/code] list. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].
The size of the Start button's text, in CSS pixels. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].
The Start button's background color while the pointer is over it. Only used while [member html/start_button/custom_state_colors] is [code]true[/code].

The space between the Start button's border and its text, in CSS pixels: [code]x[/code] on the left and right, [code]y[/code] above and below. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the files the game needs (the engine, the main pack, and the shader and texture packs this browser loads) download in the background while the start screen waits, so after the press only the engine's own startup is left. The engine itself still runs only on the press: its WebAssembly is not compiled and no GPU device is created before it. A press before the download finishes carries on with it, and nothing is downloaded twice. In the browser's Save-Data mode the download waits for the press, as without this option. This runs in the game's own page because browsers keep a separate HTTP cache for each site that embeds a page: a parent page fetching the same files would not speed up a cross-origin iframe of the game. A custom HTML shell receives this as [code]startButton.preload[/code] in [code]$GODOT_CONFIG[/code] and starts the download with [code]Engine.prototype.prefetch()[/code]. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the start screen shows the background download's progress under the button ("Downloading 48%", then "Ready"). Its messages, color, font and size are set with [code]html/start_button/preload_text/*[/code]. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload] is [code]true[/code].

The color of the download progress line under the Start button, drawn at full opacity, so the line shows exactly this color. The default, [code]#c4c4c4[/code], gives the line the look it had before this option existed (a lighter color at 85% opacity over the default boot splash background). The line keeps the default shell's text shadow. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_progress] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the progress line shows [member html/start_button/preload_text/downloading_text] while the download's total size is not known yet. If [code]false[/code], the line stays empty until the first percentage. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_progress] is [code]true[/code].
The message shown before the download's total size is known. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_text/downloading] is [code]true[/code].

The CSS [code]font-family[/code] list of the download progress line under the Start button, for example [code]'Courier New', monospace[/code]. A font the browser does not have falls back to the next one in the list. The default is the default shell's own font. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_progress] is [code]true[/code].

The font size of the download progress line under the Start button, in CSS pixels. The default, [code]14.4[/code], is the size the line had before this option existed. The line's height follows the size. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_progress] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the progress line shows [member html/start_button/preload_text/progress_text] while the files download. If [code]false[/code], the line stays empty during the download. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_progress] is [code]true[/code].

The message shown while the files download. Every [code]{percent}[/code] in it is replaced by the whole percentage downloaded so far, which never goes backwards and stays at 99 until every file has arrived; a text without [code]{percent}[/code] is shown as it is. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_text/progress] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the progress line shows [member html/start_button/preload_text/ready_text] once every file has arrived. If [code]false[/code], the line is emptied then. Nothing is shown if a download failed, since that file is downloaded again on the press. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_progress] is [code]true[/code].
The message shown once the game has downloaded. Only used while [member html/start_button/preload_text/ready] is [code]true[/code].
The Start button's background color while it is pressed. Only used while [member html/start_button/custom_state_colors] is [code]true[/code].
The text on the Start button. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].
The color of the Start button's text, also used for its keyboard focus ring. Only used while [member html/start_button/enabled] is [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows the spinner whenever the WebGPU driver compiles a shader that was not baked at export time; the number of shaders compiled so far is appended. Default: [code]true[/code].

If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows [member loading_screen/compiling_shaders/text] whenever the WebGPU driver compiles a shader that was not baked at export time; the number of shaders compiled so far is appended.

Defaults to [code]Compiling shaders...[/code]. Only used by the default HTML shell, or a [member html/custom_html_shell] that reads the [code]$GODOT_LOADING_SCREEN[/code] placeholder.

If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows [member loading_screen/initializing_engine/text] while the engine sets itself up and reads the early project settings.

If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows [member loading_screen/loading_fonts/text] while the text server and its fonts initialize.

The color of the loading screen progress bar's unfilled part. Only used while [member loading_screen/progress_bar/enabled] is [code]true[/code]. While all three progress bar colors are left at their defaults (the colors Chrome draws an unstyled bar with), the default HTML shell leaves the bar unstyled, so every browser keeps its own look; changing any of them draws the bar with all three. Only used by the default HTML shell, or a [member html/custom_html_shell] that reads the [code]$GODOT_PROGRESS_BAR[/code] placeholder.

The color of the loading screen progress bar's 1-pixel border. Only used while [member loading_screen/progress_bar/enabled] is [code]true[/code]. While all three progress bar colors are left at their defaults (the colors Chrome draws an unstyled bar with), the default HTML shell leaves the bar unstyled, so every browser keeps its own look; changing any of them draws the bar with all three. Only used by the default HTML shell, or a [member html/custom_html_shell] that reads the [code]$GODOT_PROGRESS_BAR[/code] placeholder.

If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows a progress bar that fills while the project downloads and the engine starts. If [code]false[/code], the bar is left out and the rest of the loading screen closes up around it. A [member html/custom_html_shell] receives this and the three colors as the [code]$GODOT_PROGRESS_BAR[/code] placeholder, a JSON object with [code]enabled[/code], [code]borderColor[/code], [code]backgroundColor[/code], [code]fillColor[/code] (CSS hex colors) and [code]customColors[/code] ([code]true[/code] when any color differs from its default).

The color of the loading screen progress bar's filled part. Only used while [member loading_screen/progress_bar/enabled] is [code]true[/code]. While all three progress bar colors are left at their defaults (the colors Chrome draws an unstyled bar with), the default HTML shell leaves the bar unstyled, so every browser keeps its own look; changing any of them draws the bar with all three. Only used by the default HTML shell, or a [member html/custom_html_shell] that reads the [code]$GODOT_PROGRESS_BAR[/code] placeholder.
If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows the spinner while the scene types register. Default: [code]true[/code].
If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows [member loading_screen/registering_types/text] while the scene types register.

If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows [member loading_screen/rendering_first_frame/text] while the first frame renders.

If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows [member loading_screen/starting_audio/text] while the audio server starts.

If [code]true[/code], the loading screen shows [member loading_screen/starting_renderer/text] while the rendering server starts.

The background color used behind the web application.

The [url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Manifest/display/]display mode[/url] to use for this progressive web application. Different browsers and platforms may not behave the same. - [b]Fullscreen:[/b] Displays the app in fullscreen and hides all of the browser's UI elements. - [b]Standalone:[/b] Displays the app in a separate window and hides all of the browser's UI elements. - [b]Minimal UI:[/b] Displays the app in a separate window and only shows the browser's UI elements for navigation. - [b]Browser:[/b] Displays the app as a normal web page.
If [code]true[/code], turns this web build into a [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_web_app]progressive web application[/url] (PWA).
When enabled, the progressive web app will make sure that each request has cross-origin isolation headers (COEP/COOP). This can simplify the setup to serve the exported game.
File path to the smallest icon for this web application. If not defined, defaults to the project icon. [b]Note:[/b] If the icon is not 144×144, it will be automatically resized for the final build.
File path to the small icon for this web application. If not defined, defaults to the project icon. [b]Note:[/b] If the icon is not 180×180, it will be automatically resized for the final build.
File path to the largest icon for this web application. If not defined, defaults to the project icon. [b]Note:[/b] If the icon is not 512×512, it will be automatically resized for the final build.
The page to display, should the server hosting the page not be available. This page is saved in the client's machine.

Superseded by [member html/orientation], which also sets the progressive web app manifest's orientation; this option is hidden. A preset that still sets it to [b]Landscape[/b] or [b]Portrait[/b] while [member html/orientation] is [b]Project Setting[/b] exports as Sensor Landscape or Sensor Portrait.

If [code]true[/code], the export uses occlusion culling as the project sets it ([member ProjectSettings.rendering/occlusion_culling/use_occlusion_culling]): objects hidden behind [OccluderInstance3D] occluders are not drawn, as on desktop platforms. If [code]false[/code], occlusion culling is turned off for this export only, which saves its CPU cost in scenes where little is hidden. The web export templates include the raycast module either way, so this does not change the download size.

If [code]true[/code], precompiles WebGPU shaders to WGSL at export time and ships them in the exported [code].pck[/code], instead of leaving the browser to translate SPIR-V to WGSL at load time. Only takes effect when the project's [code]rendering/rendering_device/driver.web[/code] setting is [code]webgpu[/code]; otherwise this option is a harmless no-op. Requires the editor to have been built with WebGPU support (see [code]drivers/webgpu/README.md[/code] in the source tree) — if it wasn't, export proceeds without baking and shaders fall back to the existing runtime SPIR-V to WGSL translation. [b]Note:[/b] Leaving this disabled means exported WebGPU games do significant shader-compilation work on the player's machine at load time, which can look like a freeze on first launch.

If [code]true[/code], the shaders baked by [member shader_baker/enabled] are shipped in a separate [code]<name>.shaders.pck[/code] next to the main [code].pck[/code], which the page preloads and the engine mounts at startup. The baked shaders are most of a baked [code].pck[/code] and only change when the shaders do, so a deploy that uploads whole files re-uploads much less after a code change. Requires export templates built from the same commit as the editor; an older template silently loads no baked shaders, and the export warns about it.

With [b]Automatic[/b] (the default), the shader baker leaves out the shader groups the web renderer can never select, and moves Forward+'s advanced group (motion vectors, separate specular, lightmaps, VoxelGI and SDF depth passes) into [code]<name>.shaders_extra.bin[/code] unless the project was found to use TAA, FSR 2, LightmapGI, VoxelGI, SDFGI, subsurface scattering, camera motion blur or rolling shutter, or a motion-vector compositor effect. The page fetches the extras as the engine starts, and a shader that needs one before it arrives compiles at load. With [b]Disabled[/b], every group is baked into the shader pack.

The number of threads that emscripten will allocate at startup. A smaller value will allocate fewer threads and consume fewer system resources, but you may run the risk of running out of threads in the pool and needing to allocate more threads at run time which may cause a deadlock. [b]Note:[/b] Some browsers have a hard cap on the number of threads that can be allocated, so it is best to be cautious and keep this number low.

Override for the default size of the [WorkerThreadPool]. This setting is used when [member ProjectSettings.threading/worker_pool/max_threads] size is set to [code]-1[/code] (which it is by default). This size must be smaller than [member threads/emscripten_pool_size] otherwise deadlocks may occur. When using threads, this size needs to be large enough to accommodate features that rely on having a dedicated thread like [member ProjectSettings.physics/2d/run_on_separate_thread] or [member ProjectSettings.rendering/driver/threads/thread_model]. In general, it is best to ensure that this is at least [code]4[/code] and is at least [code]2[/code] or [code]3[/code] less than [member threads/emscripten_pool_size].
If [code]true[/code] enables [GDExtension] support for this web build.

If [code]true[/code] (the default), a thread-enabled export renders on its own thread: the WebGPU device and the canvas belong to a worker, and the main thread only runs the game. Equivalent to running with [code]--render-thread separate[/code], so it takes precedence over [member ProjectSettings.rendering/driver/threads/thread_model]. Browsers that cannot use WebGPU from a worker fall back to the Safe model on their own. Has no effect unless [member variant/thread_support] is enabled, or with the WebGL renderer. If [code]false[/code], the project setting decides, as on other platforms.

If [code]true[/code], the exported game will support threads. It requires [url=https://web.dev/articles/coop-coep]a "cross-origin isolated" website[/url], which may be difficult to set up and is limited for security reasons (such as not being able to communicate with third-party websites). If [code]false[/code], the exported game will not support threads. As a result, it is more prone to performance and audio issues, but will only require to be run on an HTTPS website.
If [code]true[/code], allows textures to be optimized for desktop through the S3TC/BPTC algorithm.
If [code]true[/code] allows textures to be optimized for mobile through the ETC2/ASTC algorithm.

If [code]true[/code] and both [member vram_texture_compression/for_desktop] and [member vram_texture_compression/for_mobile] are enabled, each compression family is exported in its own [code]<name>.textures_*.pck[/code], and the page downloads only the one the device can sample instead of both. Has no effect on an encrypted pack.
